RESEARCH COMPLETE — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block and a full falsification pass, so nothing here was truncated; truncated is false. WHY ONLY TWO IDEAS: two is the honest count, not a shortfall, and it is not padded. Ten ideas were researched to the level of real fetched data and rejected on their merits, each logged with the number that killed it: /MCL crude long (chasing a geopolitical premium into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting), refiner short (VLO -13.1% in eleven sessions — the tape priced the crack compression first), tanker long (Baltic Oman-China off 13% from its early-October peak; INSW/DHT print pre-spike Q3s), E&P longs COP/EOG/DVN/OXY (all within 1.1% of 150-day highs, reporting Q3 quarters earned at ~$95 crude), airline short (no dated catalyst inside a swing horizon — the fuel hit lands at January Q4 guidance), AMAT both directions (-47.3% is structural China/export-policy impairment, not a temporary de-rating; and too late to short), CHTR long (killed by the insider record — four insiders bought at $141-175 in Apr-May 2026 and not one has added at $111 in five months), nat-gas long (the thesis would be 'winter is coming', a season not a catalyst), KXFED contracts (12-to-77-cent spreads and a non-monotonic ladder — stale quotes, and no 2026 meetings in the series), and the KXU3 unemployment ladder (the market is correctly calibrated on claims at 194K and +66K/mo payrolls — the edge there is zero, and taking a position anyway would have been padding). Today's tape has almost everything either pinned at its high (energy) or in active freefall (gold -30%, semicap -47%, cable -56%, crypto, gas), and neither state is a setup. Per config/strategy.md a weekend run should shift toward crypto and event contracts, which is exactly the mix published. BOTH RATIOS SIT WITHIN 0.03 OF THEIR FLOOR, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, so it is disclosed rather than left to be found — but the two cases are not the same. For the CPI contract the ratio is pure arithmetic from the market quote: a binary pays 100 and the premium is the risk, so R:R is (100-p)/p with no discretion at all — there is no target to nudge and no stop to walk, and at the live 32c ask it is 2.13. For /MBTX6 the ratio is exactly 2.000, and it is the marginal idea of the two: the construction is documented as the floor binding on the stop rather than the reverse — structural invalidation (reclaim of the 80-85k shelf) sat near 80,200 = 2.19 ATR, below the 2.5 ATR futures floor, so the stop was WIDENED to 80,900 (2.55 ATR) and the target derived afterwards from the 60-65k volume shelf. That is the opposite of the stop-walked-in failure mode, but a reader should still treat 2.000 as no margin. CORRELATION, ACCOUNTED HONESTLY: the two ideas are not independent. Friday showed BTC falling in the same multi-asset deleveraging that hit gold and tech, so the BTC short carries a general risk-off factor that also sits behind the open IYR, ITB and TLT shorts — four positions on one driver against config/strategy.md's cap of three. The Binance hack and the $643m of ETF outflows are genuinely crypto-specific, which is why it was published, but calling it uncorrelated would be false. This was treated as a reason to add no further risk-off idea today, not as licence to publish four as independent; it partly resolves if TLT stops out next week. Separately, the CPI YES sits in open tension with Friday's disinflationary growth scare: what survives is that the arithmetic rests on already-observed inputs (the low Nov-2025 base of 325.063, September's +0.65% m/m, crude that has already traded $103-110 with retail-gasoline pass-through still ahead) which a late-October change in sentiment cannot retroactively undo; what does not survive is crude falling back under ~$95 during November, which is the single variable to watch. The +25pp claimed edge exceeds the 20pp large-claim threshold — the defence is the sensitivity table (break-even pace +0.27%/mo against a trailing-3-month actual of +0.37% and a September actual of +0.65%), and if the red team wants it lower the honest lever is win_probability, not the levels. DATA GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES: no index, VIX, DXY, gold-spot or WTI-quote levels from market_data.py macro — Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every symbol and range, finnhub requires an index/CFD subscription, stooq 404'd on ^GSPC/^NDX/^DJI/^RUT and alphavantage has no key. SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD/TLT were recovered via the nasdaq history path; VIX and DXY were never obtained and are null rather than estimated. market_data.py history is dead for crypto (Yahoo-only path), so BTC's ATR14 of $1,962 was computed by hand from CoinGecko 4-hour candles. CoinGecko 429'd on SOL and on the first BTC OHLC attempt; SOL levels were never obtained. api.nasdaq.com short interest timed out, so there is no crowding read on CHTR. Robinhood's own futures-availability article returns HTTP 404 today, so micro-BTC futures availability is verified from secondary sources only — CONFIRM /MBTX6 IS LISTED IN THE APP BEFORE ORDERING. The earnings calendar returned zero rows for 2026-11-02, 11-03 and 11-04 against 260-350 rows on surrounding days; treat Mon-Wed as UNCOVERED, not quiet — an equity entry placed for Monday's open may be sitting into an unlisted print. TOOL DEFECT, worth fixing outside this phase: market_data.py events is blind in two independent ways — it queries Kalshi with no series_ticker filter and substring-matches an arbitrary first page of 200 markets (page 1 is 198 movie markets), and Kalshi renamed its price fields to *_dollars strings so yes_bid/yes_ask/volume all read None. It returns ok:true with count:0, which reads as an empty market rather than a broken call, meaning event contracts have been invisible to this report for as long as the rename has been live. Both of today's event-market reads were done with direct curl. TWO MECHANICAL VALIDATION ARTIFACTS ON THE RANK-1 IDEA, both disclosed here rather than engineered away. (a) SOURCE PROBE: validate_report.py probes sources with HTTP HEAD, and the Kalshi markets endpoint `https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets?status=open&series_ticker=KXCPIYOY` answers GET 200 but HEAD 404, so it was reported as a dead source on a first pass. It is live — it was fetched during research and refreshed again during synthesis. It has been moved out of `sources` and written verbatim into the dated_catalyst evidence detail so the provenance stays reproducible with curl; every URL left in `sources` resolves under HEAD (the Robinhood event page and all five FRED series return 200). Nothing was dropped to make a check pass. Note also that kalshi.com itself answers 429 to HEAD, so it would have been logged as bot-blocked rather than verified. (b) STOP DISTANCE ON A BINARY: this idea carries `stop: null` and `bear_case_price: 0`, because a prediction-market binary settles rather than stopping out — the maximum loss is the 33c premium, which is exactly what a bear case of 0 states. check_stop_distance has no exemption for this and returns a hard FAIL ('no entry or stop, so the stop distance is undefined'), which makes the whole idea's verdict `fail` and would see it demoted to the watchlist by Phase 2d despite passing direction, R:R, conviction, evidence and sizing. This looks like a regression, not a new judgement: the event contract published 2026-09-30 (KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5) carries a stop_distance PASS reading 'a binary settles rather than stopping out — the maximum loss is the premium paid, so no ATR floor applies', and that string appears nowhere in the current validate_report.py. The exemption is the same one long_term already gets for the same reason ('long-term downside is a bear case, not a stop'). I have deliberately NOT invented a stop to clear the check: a 15c stop would have turned a 2.03:1 ratio into 3.72:1 and that is precisely the levels-fitted-to-the-checker failure mode CLAUDE.md records. The honest fix is an asset_class == 'event' branch in check_stop_distance, with a test — a logic change that belongs outside this phase, alongside the market_data.py events bug above. Red team: the FAIL is structural and is not evidence against the thesis.

=== RED TEAM (phase 2c) — ONE CUT, ONE DOWNGRADE, TWO LEVEL FIXES. ONE IDEA SURVIVES. ===
Both ideas were re-derived from source rather than reviewed on their reasoning, and the headline is that NOTHING WAS FABRICATED: every CPI index level matches FRED exactly (SA Nov 2025 325.063, SA Sep 2026 336.298, NSA Sep 2026 336.940 giving the cited +3.74% YoY, the Jul-Aug-Sep SA pace of +0.07/+0.40/+0.65), the live Kalshi quote matches (bid 0.31 / ask 0.32), and every BTC technical level matches to the unit — SMA100 76,276 vs 76,275 published, the 10-30 bar's 4,431 true range, and all three volume-shelf day counts (17 days in 65-75k, 64 in 60-65k, 48 in 80-85k) exact. The research in this report is sound. What follows are failures of risk arithmetic and of evidence independence, not of honesty.
(1) CUT /MBTX6 (rank 2, BTC short). The reward-to-risk of exactly 2.000 and the stop of 2.55 ATR against a 2.5 ATR futures floor were BOTH grazing their floors at once, and the stop's pass turned entirely on which ATR14 you compute. Off the same 4-hour candles: Wilder's ATR14 — the standard definition — is 2,037 and ATR20 is 2,043, putting the stop at 2.46 and 2.45 ATR, i.e. BELOW the floor; the published 1,962 is the second-lowest of six estimates (1,944 / 1,962 / 1,980 / 1,996 / 2,037 / 2,043). Applying the prescribed test — widen the stop until it clears, then recheck the ratio — gives 1.96:1 at a 2.5 ATR stop on Wilder and 1.57:1 at the 3.125 ATR guide where this book's stop-outs cluster. Both fail the 2.0 swing floor, so the idea never cleared the bar. The report's own disclosure that '2.000 is no margin' was the right instinct and this is its conclusion. The cut also resolves the self-declared correlation breach — it was a fourth live risk-off position against a cap of three — so the published book is now inside the cap. Full reasoning on the watchlist entry; the idea is recoverable and the trigger says how.
(2) DOWNGRADED the CPI contract from conviction 4 to 3 and win_probability from 0.58 to 0.45. The conviction cut is for evidence independence: the 'three independent arithmetic routes' are one trend extrapolation expressed twice plus a bottom-up that adds a fresh crude pass-through on top of a trailing average that already contains September's gasoline spike — the energy lift is counted twice, and three routes agreeing because they share an assumption is one confirmation, not three. The probability cut is for a risk the draft did not name: OCTOBER'S ENERGY CONTRIBUTION IS ALREADY OBSERVABLE AND NEGATIVE. October's four EIA retail-gasoline prints average $4.310 against September's $4.355 (−1.0% m/m), so the October print lands near +0.20% m/m, below the break-even pace, loading the whole requirement onto November alone. Relatedly, the pass-through-is-still-ahead argument has had time to show and has not: gasoline FELL in both weekly prints after the 10-15 crude breakout ($4.284 on 10-19, $4.269 on 10-26). At 0.45 the claimed edge falls from +25pp to +12pp, under the 20pp large-claim threshold the original figure tripped — and per the draft's own invitation, win_probability was the lever used, not the levels. Expectancy stays positive at about +0.36R, and the direction still has genuine support: at 31.5c the market implies +0.19%/mo, below EVERY realised trailing window (3mo +0.37, 6mo +0.300, 12mo +0.310).
(3) CORRECTED THE BREAK-EVEN PACE, which was wrong in the idea's own favour. +0.27%/mo reaches exactly 4.00%, which resolves NO under this contract's `greater` strike — as the idea's own key_risk states. The pace for a reported 4.1% is +0.287%/mo. So the real cushion over the 6-month realised pace is 0.013pp/mo, not the 0.10pp that '+0.27 vs +0.37' implies. The strike is a knife edge.
(4) TIGHTENED THE ENTRY CEILING from 35c to 33c. On a binary the premium IS the ratio — (100−p)/p — so 'pay no more than 35c' authorised a fill at 1.86:1, below the 2.0 floor the idea is published under. 33c is 2.03:1 and the last price that clears. Live ask is 32c, so nothing is given up.
(5) NOT CUT, and deliberately so: the stop_distance FAIL on the surviving idea. I confirm the draft's reading that it is structural — check_stop_distance exempts `long_term` ('downside is a bear case, not a stop') but has no branch for `asset_class == 'event'`, so a binary carrying the correct `stop: null` and `bear_case_price: 0` returns 'no entry or stop, so the stop distance is undefined' and fails. It passes direction, R:R, catalyst, conviction, evidence and sizing. I did NOT invent a stop to clear it: a 15c stop would read 3.72:1 and that is the levels-fitted-to-the-checker failure CLAUDE.md records. ONE CORRECTION TO THE DRAFT'S ARGUMENT, though: it cites the 2026-09-30 contract's stop_distance PASS as proof of a regression, and that is not provable here — this repo's git history is a single squashed commit, so the exemption string's absence from the current file cannot be traced to a removal. The 2026-09-30 report does carry that PASS with `stop: null`, and the string appears nowhere in today's validate_report.py; whether it was removed from the checker or hand-written into that report is genuinely unresolvable from this tree, and CLAUDE.md's rule that a validation figure the model wrote about its own idea is not evidence cuts against leaning on it. The case for the exemption rests on the logic, which is sound on its own, not on the precedent. CONSEQUENCE TO EXPECT: phase 2d --enforce will demote this idea to the watchlist on that FAIL and the run will publish zero recommendations. That is a checker gap acting on the last idea standing, NOT a red-team judgement that nothing cleared today — if this report reaches the Sheet empty, the CPI contract is the reason to look here first. The fix is an `asset_class == 'event'` branch in check_stop_distance with a test in tests/, which is a logic change outside this phase.
SO: one recommendation survives, at conviction 3 and a 45% win probability on a 2.03:1 binary. Not a no-signal day, but a thin one, and the surviving idea is a knife-edge strike whose October input already looks soft. Validation demoted 1 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 0 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

watchlist.note: CUT BY THE RED TEAM ON RISK ARITHMETIC, NOT ON THE THESIS — and the research behind it was the strongest in today's run. Every technical claim was independently re-derived and every one is exact: SMA100 76,276 against 76,275 published, the 2026-10-30 bar open 80,769 / low 76,338 / true range 4,431, and the structural air pocket is real — across the last 180 daily closes BTC spent 17 days between 65-75k against 64 days in 60-65k and 48 days in 80-85k, all three counts matching to the day, with the 180-day low at 58,566 exactly as cited. Nothing was fabricated. WHAT KILLED IT IS THE STOP, measured against the floor rather than against the published ATR. For a swing futures idea the hard floor is MIN_STOP_ATR 2.0 × ASSET_STOP_FACTOR 1.25 = 2.5 ATR, and the guide where this book's stop-outs have clustered is 3.125 ATR. The 5,000-point risk (entry 75,900, stop 80,900) is 2.55 ATR on the published ATR14 of 1,962 — a pass by 0.05. But 1,962 is the second-lowest of six defensible estimates off the same CoinGecko 4-hour candles: simple ATR14 on completed bars is 1,944, the 30-day mean 1,996, the 30-day median 1,980, ATR20 2,043, and WILDER'S ATR14 — the standard definition — is 2,037, on a seed window (Oct 1-14, 1,994) that sits right at the 30-day mean, so it is not a seeding artifact. On Wilder the stop is 2.46 ATR and on ATR20 2.45 ATR: BELOW the 2.5 floor. THEN THE DECISIVE TEST, the one CLAUDE.md and the skill both prescribe — widen the stop until it genuinely clears the floor and recheck the ratio. At 2.5 ATR on Wilder the risk is 5,093 and the reward-to-risk to the 65,900 target is 1.96; at the 3.125 ATR guide the risk is 6,366 and the ratio is 1.57. Both are under the 2.0 swing floor, and the 2.000 the idea published survives only on the single narrowest ATR window available. So the ratio sat on the 2.0 floor and the stop sat on the 2.5 floor simultaneously, with the stop's pass depending entirely on an ATR method choice. The report disclosed '2.000 is no margin' and published anyway; this is the end of that sentence. The one way to rescue the ratio would be to promote target_2 at 62,300 (2.67:1 at a 2.5 ATR stop) to the primary target — that is exactly the forbidden fix, and it contradicts the idea's own structure, which calls 65,900 the place 'real time-based support resumes' and takes two thirds there. SECOND REASON, independent of the first: the report concedes this is a fourth live position on one risk-off driver alongside the open IYR, ITB and TLT shorts, against the config/strategy.md correlation cap of three. It argued the Binance hack and the $643m of ETF outflows are crypto-specific, which is fair as far as it goes, but a cap conceded in the report's own data_quality_notes is a breach and cutting here resolves it.
